### 1. Project

This RFP is for one engagement, Building services engineering, covering Mechanical services, Electrical services, Hydraulic services and Fire services. One agreement covers every discipline. You may deliver any discipline yourself or through a subconsultant you name in R4. Price each discipline in the fee schedule (section 3).

Example Client intends to build Office (Class 5) at 1 Example Street, Example NSW.

| The building | Site and planning | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| Work type: New build | Site address: 1 Example Street, Example NSW | Client: Example Client |
| Building: Office: Class 5 | Planning pathway: Development application (DA) | Procurement route: Traditional lump sum; continuation/novation requires separate appointment. |

Conditions that do not apply: Work to an existing building.

### 2. Scope of services

This engagement covers 4 disciplines. Each part below is that discipline's scope, as it would be issued alone. An item one discipline's scope gives to another discipline in this engagement is shown once, under the discipline that does it, marked within this engagement.

### 2.1 Mechanical services

You are the mechanical services engineer. Your job is to keep the occupants comfortable and healthy, with the right temperatures, fresh air and ventilation, using plant that fits the building, meets the energy targets and can be maintained.
To do this you:
- Set the design loads and plant strategy early, and give the architect and structural engineer the space, weight and penetrations the plant needs.
- Design the selected systems to the level of detail each appointed stage buys, with load, airflow, pressure and selection calculations.
- Show how the outdoor-air requirement is met: air conditioning is not fresh air.
- Say what loads or evidence are missing and resolve them before relying on them.
For the office or retail space, this includes zoning that tenants can adapt and the energy rating the brief targets.
The fire engineer owns the fire strategy and Performance Solutions; you design the selected plant and its fire modes to suit them. Trades install, program and test. Your reviews and witnessing are not their work, continuous supervision, or certification of work you did not see.

### 2.2 Electrical services

You are the electrical services engineer. Your job is to give the building safe, reliable power, lighting and communications that suit how it is used, fit the supply available, and can be built and maintained.
To do this you:
- Confirm the supply early: the load, the capacity available and what the network operator needs. Never assume spare capacity.
- Design the selected systems to the level of detail each appointed stage buys.
- Keep the measured, utility and calculated basis of the design, and registers of utility matters, deliverables and decisions.
For the office or retail space, this includes tenancy metering and capacity set aside for tenants' fit-outs.
Power to process equipment is not process design. The network operator, its accredited service provider (Level 3), the ICT operator and the contractors keep their own duties. Your reviews and witnessing are not installation testing or certification.

### 2.3 Hydraulic services

You are the hydraulic services engineer. Your job is to give the building safe, reliable water, drainage and gas services that meet the authorities' requirements, suit how the building is used, and can be maintained.
To do this you:
- Confirm the authorities' connection requirements and the capacity of existing services early.
- Provide coordinated hydraulic design for the selected services and stages, with calculations, drawings, schedules and design-basis records.
- For each shared connection, name who owns its design, evidence, installation, controls, testing and acceptance.
- Resolve gaps before anyone relies on the design.
For the office or retail space, this includes tenancy metering and connections left ready for food and other tenant fit-outs.

### 2.4 Fire services

You are the fire services engineer. Your job is to design the fire systems allocated to you so they protect occupants and property, deliver the fire strategy, meet the authority's requirements, and can be tested and maintained.
To do this you:
- Confirm the water supply and the authority's requirements early.
- Design the selected systems to the level of detail each appointed stage buys.
- Coordinate space, tanks, pumps and penetrations with the architect, structural and other services engineers.
A concept tank and pump capacity is not full hydraulic design or proof that the existing supply is adequate.
The fire engineer owns the fire strategy and Performance Solutions; authorities decide. Trades install, test and certify. Your reviews and witnessing neither carry out tests nor certify work you did not see. Name who owns network design and authority applications.
Design basis: R7: parts/use/hazards, strategy/approvals, insurer/operator criteria, records/revisions, supply dates/conditions, plant/pipework and access gaps.
